title: There Is a Book, Who Runs May Read
description: There Is a Book, Who Runs May Read in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Keble wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 476, “The Elder Scripture”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: There is a book, who runs may read, Which heav-enly truth im-parts; And all the lore its schol-ars need, Pure eyes and lov-ing hearts.

lines: There is a book, who runs may read,
Which heavenly truth imparts;
And all the lore its scholars need,
Pure eyes and loving hearts.
The works of God, above, below,
Within us, and around,
Are pages in that book, to show
How God himself is found.
The glorious sky, embracing all,
Is like the Father's love;
Wherewith encompassed, great and small
In peace and order move.
The dew of heaven is like His grace;
It steals in silence down;
But where it lights, the favored place
By richest fruits is known.
Two worlds are ours; 'tis only sin
Forbids us to descry
The mystic heaven and earth within,
Plain as the earth and sky.
Thou, who hast given me eyes to see
And love this sight so fair,
Give me a heart to find out Thee,
And read Thee everywhere!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Keble died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Keble (1792–1866), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
